name: SystemVerilog
designers: Accellera (Co-Design Automation SUPERLOG donation, Synopsys Vera/OpenVera donation)
summary: Hardware design and verification language standardised as IEEE 1800 (2005, 2009, 2012, 2017, 2023); a superset of Verilog adding rich data types, interfaces, packages, a class-based object system with constrained randomisation, functional coverage and SystemVerilog Assertions. Since 2009 IEEE 1800 subsumes IEEE 1364 Verilog.

level_notes.1: IEEE 1800 is the normative definition; the standard is paywalled but IEEE 1800 (and 1800.2 UVM) is free of charge through the IEEE GET Program (registration). No open working draft is linked; implementation manuals (Verilator, slang, Yosys) are filed at level 2 as they document tool support, not the language.
level_notes.0: No reference implementation. Open implementations: Verilator (compiled simulator), slang (complete front end/elaborator), Surelog/UHDM (parser with ANTLR grammar), Verible (parser/linter), sv2v (SV-to-Verilog converter), Yosys (synthesisable subset), CIRCT Moore dialect; the sv-tests suite measures conformance across tools.
level_notes.2: Free tutorials (ChipVerify, ASIC World, Doulos, Verification Guide) and many freely downloadable conference papers (Sutherland, Cummings); the main books (Sutherland et al., Spear & Tumbush) are commercial.
